chunks: Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad, the jurisprudent in Balkh, informed me of what he authorized for me, saying: Abu Harb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Aheed narrated to us from Ibn Abi Isa al-Hafiz, saying: Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Bakir narrated to us, saying: Al-Lays narrated from Ibn al-Had, from Abdullah ibn Khabab, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, saying:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The congregational prayer is superior to the individual prayer by twenty-five degrees.'
And my father (may God be pleased with him) said in his letter to me: 'For the man's prayer in congregation over the man's prayer alone, there are twenty-five degrees in Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward difference between congregational prayer and individual prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal underscores the communal nature of worship in Shia tradition, where the collective act of prayer amplifies individual devotion by twenty-five degrees. The inclusion of the narrator's father's corroboration highlights the reliability of the chain (isnad) and reinforces the practical emphasis on congregational unity (jama'ah) as a means of spiritual elevation.
